info.title: spring
info.description: Spring Voyage CLI — operator and end-user command-line client for the Spring Voyage AI agent collaboration platform. Talks to a deployed Spring Voyage API (set SPRING_API_URL); supports unit/agent/secret/connector/system commands. See https://github.com/cvoya-com/spring-voyage for the full platform.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Create a new agent

options.name: --name
options.description: Human-readable display name. Required — agent identity is assigned by the platform (ADR-0039 §8).

options.name: --description
options.description: Optional human-readable description for the agent.

options.name: --unit
options.description: Unit to add the agent to. Repeat to assign multiple units; omit to create a top-level tenant-parented agent.

options.name: --definition-file
options.description: Path to a JSON file containing the agent definition document (e.g. execution.tool/image/provider/model). When supplied, its contents are sent verbatim to the server and persisted on AgentDefinitions.Definition.

options.name: --definition
options.description: Inline JSON literal for the agent definition document. Alternative to --definition-file.

options.name: --from-package
options.description: Install an agent from a package in the catalog. Provide the package name. Mutually exclusive with --inherit, --definition, --definition-file, and execution shorthand flags (full validation in L6).

options.name: --connector
options.description: Connector binding for the package install. Format: <slug>=<binding-id> or <slug>. Repeat to bind multiple connectors. Only valid with --from-package; errors when used alone.

options.name: --input
options.description: Package install input (legacy). Format: <key>=<value>. Repeat to set multiple inputs. Only valid with --from-package; errors when used alone.

options.name: --image
options.description: Container image reference (shorthand for execution.image on the agent definition).

options.name: --runtime
options.description: Agent runtime id (shorthand for execution.runtime; e.g. claude-code, codex, gemini, spring-voyage).

options.name: --model-provider
options.description: Model-provider id (shorthand for execution.model.provider; e.g. anthropic, openai, google, ollama). Required for multi-provider runtimes (spring-voyage); optional for fixed-provider runtimes (must match the implied provider when supplied).

options.name: --model
options.description: Model id (shorthand for execution.model.id; e.g. claude-opus-4-7).

options.name: --hosting
options.description: Hosting mode (shorthand for execution.hosting). Allowed values: ephemeral, persistent.

options.name: --inherit
options.description: Omit all execution fields; the agent inherits its runtime, model, image, and hosting from its parent unit(s).

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Print stack traces and additional diagnostics on failure

options.name: --verbose

commands.name: execution
commands.description: Read / write the agent's on-disk execution block. Fields: image, runtime, model-provider, model, hosting, system-prompt-mode. Missing fields fall back to the parent unit's execution defaults at dispatch time (system-prompt-mode further falls back to the platform default 'append' when no unit value is declared).

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Print stack traces and additional diagnostics on failure

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Remove the agent's execution block (or a single field when --field is set). Pass --system-prompt-mode to clear just the prompt-shaping slot via PATCH; that flag is independent of --field and does not touch the execution block.

commands.name: get
commands.description: Print the agent's own declared execution block. Does NOT show inherited unit defaults for image / runtime / model / hosting — null fields indicate either an unset agent-level slot or a slot that will resolve from the parent unit at dispatch. For system-prompt-mode both the declared (agent-own) and effective (post-cascade) values are printed so operators can see what the dispatcher will actually use.

commands.name: set
commands.description: Upsert one or more fields on the agent's execution block. Partial update — pass only the flags you want to change. The system-prompt-mode slot rides a separate PATCH (it lives on the agent's persisted definition rather than the execution shape) but the CLI exposes it here for symmetry with the other prompt-pipeline knobs.

arguments.name: id-or-name
arguments.description: The agent's stable Guid (32-char no-dash hex or dashed form), OR a display_name to search for. When a name is supplied and multiple agents match, a disambiguation list is printed with each candidate's Guid.

commands.name: skills
commands.description: Equip / unequip / list the skill bundles on this agent (#2361). Bundles are addressed by <pkg>/<skill> — no @version, no aliases.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Print stack traces and additional diagnostics on failure

commands.name: add
commands.description: Equip a single skill bundle on the agent. Idempotent — re-adding refreshes the persisted prompt + required-tools snapshot without reordering.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the skill bundles equipped on the agent. Bundles render in declaration order — the first row renders first in Layer 4 of the assembled prompt.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Unequip a single skill bundle from the agent. No-op when the bundle is not currently equipped.

commands.name: set
commands.description: Bulk-replace the agent's equipped skill bundles. The API has no atomic bulk write — the CLI composes the diff (remove dropped, add new); a mid-flight failure leaves the subject in a partially-applied state.

options.name: --verbose

commands.name: costs
commands.description: Cost rollup over a window. Defaults to the tenant total; pass --unit or --agent to scope.

options.name: --window
options.description: Rollup window, e.g. '24h', '7d', '30d', '90d'. Defaults to '30d' when unset.

options.name: --unit
options.description: Filter the rollup to a specific unit (mutually exclusive with --agent).

options.name: --agent
options.description: Filter the rollup to a specific agent (mutually exclusive with --unit).

options.name: --by-source
options.description: Show cost broken down by source (agent / unit). Calls the dashboard costs endpoint and prints a per-source table. When combined with --agent, shows the per-model breakdown for that agent instead (hits the agent breakdown endpoint). --unit is ignored when --by-source is set.

options.name: --series
options.description: Show cost as a bucketed time-series (sparkline data). Requires --agent or --unit. Use --bucket to select bucket size (1h, 1d, 7d; default 1d) and --window to control the time span (default 30d).

commands.description: Manage connector bindings for units

options.name: --verbose

commands.name: bind
commands.description: Bind a unit to a connector and upsert its per-unit config. Mirrors the portal's unit Connector tab.

options.name: --unit
options.description: The unit identifier (Guid) to bind to a connector.

options.name: --type
options.description: The connector type slug (e.g. 'github'). Must match a slug reported by 'spring connector catalog'.

options.name: --repo
options.description: GitHub repository in qualified 'owner/repo' form (required when --type github). Per ADR-0047 §11 the binding's addressing concern is the qualified pair, not the owner and repo names as separate columns.

options.name: --installation-id
options.description: GitHub App installation id (App-installation auth path per ADR-0047 §6). Mutually exclusive with --pat-secret-name — exactly one of the two MUST be set at binding-create time per ADR-0047 §11.

options.name: --pat-secret-name
options.description: Tenant-secret name addressing the PAT this binding pushes with (PAT auth path per ADR-0047 §§ 5–6). The default naming convention is 'binding/<binding-id-no-dash>/github/pat'; operators who paste an existing secret name override it. Mutually exclusive with --installation-id — exactly one of the two MUST be set at binding-create time per ADR-0047 §11.

options.name: --events
options.description: Optional webhook events to subscribe to. Repeatable. When omitted the server falls back to the connector's default event set.

options.name: --reviewer
options.description: Optional default reviewer (GitHub login) used for human-review handoffs on this unit. When omitted the connector falls back to its installation default.

options.name: --include-label
options.description: Inbound webhook filter: only deliver events whose subject carries one of these labels. Repeat or comma-separate. Issue #2407.

options.name: --exclude-label
options.description: Inbound webhook filter: drop events whose subject carries one of these labels (evaluated first). Repeat or comma-separate. Issue #2407.

options.name: --include-author
options.description: Inbound webhook filter: only deliver events authored by one of these GitHub logins. Repeat or comma-separate. Issue #2407.

options.name: --include-path
options.description: Inbound webhook filter: only deliver PR-shape events whose changed files match one of these path prefixes. Repeat or comma-separate. Issue #2407.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Print stack traces and additional diagnostics on failure

commands.name: install
commands.description:
Install one or more packages from the catalog (spring package install <name> [<name>...]) or from a local file (spring package install --file <path>).
For single-target installs, supply inputs as bare key=value pairs: --input github_owner=acme.
For multi-target installs, namespace inputs by package: --input <pkg>.key=value.
Alternatively supply a YAML file via --input-file.
Required connectors: supply with --connector <slug>=<owner>/<repo>@<installation-id> (github short form) or --connector <slug>.<key>=<value> (long form, generic). Per-unit override: --connector <slug>:<unit-name>=...
Version pinning (ADR-0037 D5): use --version <v> to install a specific package version. When omitted the install resolves to the most recently installed version.
Display name (#2310): use --as <name> to override the display name of the package's single top-level activatable. Useful when installing the same package multiple times.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 2 = bad request / dep-graph error, 1 = server error.

options.name: --file
options.description: Path to a local package YAML file. Installs the package from the file rather than the catalog (one-shot upload; ADR-0035 decision 13). Mutually exclusive with positional names.

options.name: --input
options.description: Input value for a package, repeatable. For a single-target install use bare key=value: --input github_owner=acme. For a multi-target install namespace by package: --input <pkg>.key=value. Mixing bare and namespaced forms in the same invocation is an error.

options.name: --input-file
options.description: Path to a YAML file supplying package inputs. For single-target installs the file's top-level keys are input names. For multi-target installs the file's top-level keys are package names and each nested map's keys are input names.

options.name: --connector
options.description: Connector binding for a required package connector, repeatable. Short form (github only today): --connector github=owner/repo@installation-id. Per-unit override: --connector github:unit-name=owner/repo@installation-id. Long form (any connector): --connector github.installation-id=12345 --connector github.owner=acme. For multi-target installs, namespace by package: --connector <pkg>.<slug>=... or <pkg>.<slug>.<key>=value.

options.name: --version
options.description: Pin the install to a specific package version (ADR-0037 D5). When omitted, the install resolves to the most recently installed version of the package. For multi-target installs, supply once per target name in declaration order.

options.name: --secret
options.description: LLM credential for the package's runtimes, repeatable. Form: --secret <provider>:<auth-method>=<value> (e.g. --secret anthropic:oauth=sk-ant-oat-... or --secret openai:api-key=sk-...). For multi-target installs, namespace by package: --secret <pkg>.<provider>:<auth-method>=<value>. Required credentials missing from the request prompt the operator interactively when stdin is a TTY; otherwise the install fails with a structured CredentialsMissing error listing each missing slot.

options.name: --into
options.description: Bind the package's top-level artefacts to the named unit instead of the tenant (ADR-0043 §6). Accepts a unit display name or Guid. Use --into tenant for the explicit default. Applies to every target in a multi-target install.

options.name: --as
options.description: Override the display name of the package's single top-level activatable (#2310). Useful when installing the same package multiple times. Applies to every target in a multi-target install. Rejected when any target's package ships more than one top-level activatable.

options.name: --as-human
options.description: Per-declaration Human → TenantUser binding override (ADR-0062 § 6 / #2822). Form: --as-human <declaration-display-name>=<tenant-user-ref>. Repeatable for multiple slots. The declaration key matches the package's `- human: { displayName: ... }` field case-sensitively. <tenant-user-ref> accepts a UUID, 'me' (= calling caller), or an OAuth subject of an existing TenantUser in the current tenant. For multi-target installs, namespace by package: --as-human <pkg>.<decl>=<ref>.

commands.name: create
commands.description:
Create a new unit.
By default waits for backend validation to finish (polls GET /api/v1/units/{name} once per second until the unit reaches Stopped or Error). Pass --no-wait to return immediately after the create is accepted. Progress in the CLI is coarse — a single "Validating..." indicator until terminal; the web portal renders per-step progress via the SSE channel.
Inline credentials are auth-method specific: use --oauth-token / --oauth-token-from-file for claude-code, and --api-key / --api-key-from-file for API-key edges such as codex, gemini, and spring-voyage with anthropic/openai/google. spring-voyage with ollama accepts no credential flags.
Exit codes:
0   Success
1   Unknown/other error
2   Usage error (bad flags or invalid state for the operation)
20  ImagePullFailed         22  ToolMissing         24  CredentialFormatRejected
21  ImageStartFailed        23  CredentialInvalid   25  ModelNotFound
26  ProbeTimeout        27  ProbeInternalError
Defaults to --wait (polls until terminal). Pass --no-wait to return immediately.

commands.name: revalidate
commands.description:
Re-run backend validation for a unit currently in Error or Stopped.
By default waits for validation to finish (polls GET /api/v1/units/{id} once per second until the unit reaches Stopped or Error). Pass --no-wait to return immediately after the 202 Accepted. Progress in the CLI is coarse — a single "Validating..." indicator until terminal; the web portal renders per-step progress via the SSE channel. Rejected with exit code 2 when the unit is in any other state (Running, Starting, ...).
Exit codes:
0   Success
1   Unknown/other error
2   Usage error (bad flags or invalid state for the operation)
20  ImagePullFailed         22  ToolMissing         24  CredentialFormatRejected
21  ImageStartFailed        23  CredentialInvalid   25  ModelNotFound
26  ProbeTimeout        27  ProbeInternalError
Defaults to --wait (polls until terminal). Pass --no-wait to return immediately.

options.name: --no-wait

commands.description: Run a GitHub OAuth authorization flow for the calling TenantUser (ADR-0047 §13). Opens the browser, listens on a loopback URL for the callback, and persists the OAuth-issued token as a tenant secret under the §5 binding-scoped name. The persisted secret name is printed so subsequent 'spring connector bind --pat-secret-name <name>' calls can wire the binding directly. Also refreshes the calling TenantUser's GitHub 'username' from the OAuth user-info response.

The named Hat must be bound to your TenantUser via humans.tenant_user_id; an unbound Hat returns a CLI-friendly 400. Reply composers continue to pin the Hat the thread came in on regardless of this value (ADR-0062 § 5).
